answer_text:
Let  
\[
f(T)=T^4+T^3+1\in \mathbb{F}_2[T].
\]
By definition, \(\alpha\) is a root of \(f\), i.e.
\[
\alpha^4+\alpha^3+1=0.
\]

First note that \(f\) is irreducible over \(\mathbb{F}_2\). It has no root in \(\mathbb{F}_2\) because
\[
f(0)=1,\qquad f(1)=1+1+1=1.
\]
The only monic irreducible quadratic over \(\mathbb{F}_2\) is \(T^2+T+1\). Modulo \(T^2+T+1\), we have \(T^2=T+1\), so
\[
T^3=1,\qquad T^4=T.
\]
Thus
\[
f(T)\equiv T+1+1=T\pmod{T^2+T+1},
\]
so \(T^2+T+1\) does not divide \(f\). Hence \(f\) is irreducible.

Now work in \(\mathbb{F}_{16}\). Since the characteristic is \(2\), the Frobenius map \(u\mapsto u^2\) fixes \(\mathbb{F}_2\). Therefore
\[
f(\alpha^2)=(\alpha^2)^4+(\alpha^2)^3+1=\alpha^8+\alpha^6+1.
\]
But
\[
f(\alpha)^2=(\alpha^4+\alpha^3+1)^2=\alpha^8+\alpha^6+1=f(\alpha^2).
\]
Since \(f(\alpha)=0\), we get
\[
f(\alpha^2)=0.
\]

So \(\alpha^2\) is a root of the irreducible polynomial \(f(T)\). Hence its minimal polynomial over \(\mathbb{F}_2\) is exactly \(f(T)\).

\[
\boxed{x^4+x^3+1}
